bug_description.original: Crash Type: Heap-double-free Crash Address: 0x603000007f70 Crash State: ares_parse_soa_reply ares-test-fuzz.c ares_parse_soa_reply
bug_description.normalized: In ares_parse_soa_reply, the variable rr_name is declared at function scope and allocated via ares__expand_name_for_response inside the answer-record loop. At the end of each iteration, rr_name is freed but not set to NULL. On the next iteration, if ares__expand_name_for_response fails (e.g., because the DNS buffer is exhausted), it returns an error without modifying rr_name, which still holds the dangling pointer from the previous iteration. The error handler then calls ares_free(rr_name), double-freeing the already-freed allocation.

source.description: First loop iteration: ares__expand_name_for_response parses the answer record name from the attacker-controlled DNS response buffer, allocating a heap buffer and storing the pointer in rr_name. This pointer becomes vulnerability-relevant when it is freed without being set to NULL, persisting as a dangling pointer into the next iteration.
source.value_from: Attacker-controlled DNS response buffer; the answer record name at the current aptr offset is expanded via ares_expand_name which calls malloc to allocate the name string.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: Second loop iteration error path: ares_free(rr_name) is called on the dangling pointer that was already freed at line 164 in the previous iteration. This is the double-free detected by AddressSanitizer.

root_cause.description: First free of rr_name at the end of the loop iteration without setting rr_name to NULL afterwards. The fix adds rr_name = NULL at the start of each iteration so that a failed ares__expand_name_for_response leaves rr_name as NULL rather than a dangling pointer.

parser_admitted.description: After all DNS header validation passes (alen >= HFIXEDSZ, qdcount == 1, ancount > 0, query name expansion succeeds, qclass/ancount checks pass), the answer record parsing loop begins.

tainted_value_origin.description: The heap pointer rr_name is allocated by ares__expand_name_for_response (via ares_expand_name → malloc) to hold the expanded DNS answer record name parsed from the attacker-controlled buffer.

fine_trace.note: Parses the answer count from the attacker-controlled DNS response header (big-endian uint16 at buffer offset 6). The PoC sets ancount to 5873 (>= 2), enabling multiple iterations of the answer-record loop. At least two iterations are required for the double-free: the first iteration allocates and frees rr_name, and the second iteration's failed expansion triggers the double-free.

First loop iteration (i=0): ares__expand_name_for_response successfully expands the answer record name from the DNS buffer, calling ares_expand_name which mallocs a 12-byte heap buffer and stores the pointer in rr_name. This is the allocation that will be double-freed.

End of first iteration: rr_name is freed because the parsed record has rr_type=1 (A), not T_SOA (6), so the SOA branch at line 112 is not taken. After ares_free, rr_name retains the dangling heap pointer (0x6020000001f0). The missing obligation is rr_name = NULL after this free; without it, the stale pointer persists into the next loop iteration. The fix inserts rr_name = NULL at the top of each iteration.

Second loop iteration (i=1): aptr equals abuf + alen (the first record consumed all remaining bytes). Inside ares_expand_name, name_length checks encoded >= abuf + alen, which is true, so it returns -1. ares_expand_name returns ARES_EBADNAME without modifying *s (rr_name). ares__expand_name_for_response converts the status to ARES_EBADRESP. rr_name still holds the dangling pointer from step 2.

Error handler for the failed name expansion: ares_free(rr_name) is called on the dangling pointer (0x6020000001f0) that was already freed at step 2 (line 164). AddressSanitizer detects the double-free and aborts. With the fix (rr_name = NULL at the top of the loop), this ares_free call would receive NULL and be a no-op.

format.name: DNS response
format.contract: A 40-byte binary DNS response with qdcount=1 and ancount >= 2. The query section uses DNS name compression (2-byte pointer) and is successfully expandable. The single answer section contains a non-SOA record (rr_type=A, rr_class=IN) whose name encoding (8 bytes with compression pointer), RRFIXEDSZ (10 bytes), and rr_len (4 bytes) together consume exactly the remaining buffer after the query section, so aptr equals abuf + alen at the start of the second loop iteration. The second iteration's ares__expand_name_for_response call fails because encoded >= abuf + alen in name_length, returning an error without modifying rr_name, which triggers the double-free of the stale pointer from the first iteration.
